title: Cache prepared media by timeline and transformation recipe

definition.title: Cache prepared media by timeline and transformation recipe
definition.source_excerpt: Caching · New optimization hypothesis · P2 · Risk: Medium First environment: Demuxe source + browser. Dependencies: R01. Status: Untested hypothesis. Proposed mechanism. Cache bounded already-generated fragments and initialization data for repeated seeks/replays. Key by immutable source identity, selected tracks, decoder/encoder profile, timeline origin and exact runtime recipe; do not reuse only by URL and time. Source basis. FFmpeg exposes fragmented output, while MSE can reuse valid media segments in a reconstructed presentation. The cache policy and correctness key are proposed Demuxe work. [F1, M1] First agent experiment. Replay a recently converted interval, switch away/back to the same audio, and replace a source at the same URL. Compare generated work, seek delay and total retained bytes against the uncached path.
definition.impact_basis: Potentially removes substantial work from an eligible playback, seek, preparation, retention or repeated interaction. Scope comes from the cited card; exposure and effect size are unmeasured.

definition.primary_metric: Decision power, reproducibility or diagnostic cost without changing the measured player outcome.
definition.scope_contract: Independent known truth plus a specific expected observation, not self-reported counters from the candidate.
definition.negative_control: A different failure, stale source/hash or malformed record must not count as the intended finding.
definition.stop_boundary: No dashboard, generic planner or broad testing framework. Retain a small reproducible assertion and move to the next item.
definition.shared_prerequisite: Existing fixtures and minimal observation surface; instrumentation overhead must be recorded separately.
definition.reopen_condition: A new applicable workload, resolved prerequisite, better independent oracle, or materially different bounded implementation changes the recorded decision.
